- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < 0.05) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce peak value by 5–10% to account for market overreaction.
- In periods with strong mean reversion signals (sentiment oscillating near 0.00–0.10), model often underestimates reversal magnitude; add 2–5% buffer to forecast mean.
- When sentiment is positive and price is trending upward, model frequently underestimates continuation; increase forecast slope by 1–3% relative to recent trend.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome by 2–5% over 30-day horizon, consider adding 1–2% upward bias to compensate for lagged momentum.
- In high volatility periods (sentiment extremes > 0.20 or < -0.30), model tends to over-smooth; allow 1–3% asymmetric adjustment toward true sentiment direction.
